prompt:
The table below shows how land was used in one region in 1990, 2005 and 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Land use in one region, 1990-2020 (percentage of total area)
visual.alt: A table showing the percentage of total area taken up by five types of land in one region for 1990, 2005 and 2020; each column adds up to 100.

key_points: Farmland has the largest share in all three periods but falls from 52% to 36%, a drop of 16 points — the biggest fall
Built-up land rises from 12% to 26%, more than doubling; most of the increase happens between 2005 and 2020
Forest and woodland grows steadily in every period (21% → 24% → 28%) and moves into second place by 2020
Wetland and other open land are small and almost static; both fall to 5% by 2020, ending up equal
The overall pattern: as farmland shrinks, both built-up land and forest grow, so the distribution becomes increasingly balanced across the three periods
Each column totals 100%; the table gives the share, not the actual size of the area
common_mistakes: Describing a percentage share as if it were an area ('the region lost 16 hectares of farmland')
Reading through all fifteen cells one by one instead of summarising the three main trends (farmland ↓, built-up land ↑, forest ↑)
Skipping the middle year (2005) and comparing only the first and last years — this misses how the change speeds up
Never mentioning the small, static categories (wetland, other open land)
Adding a cause or a prediction ('farmers sold their land to builders')
